item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-8980ffe7648846b6","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL documented that Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro operated nationwide, with 444,585 young people served in 2020, 63.47% receiving training certificates against a 63.25% target, and coverage at 111.15% of the annual target. The program provided scholarships, medical insurance, and training certificates, and prohibited politically electoral proselytism among training activities.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The evaluation covers 2020-2021, preceding but informing AMLO's 2023 program continuity.","ruler_attribution":"The program was a federal priority implemented under AMLO's administration.","limitations":["The document does not establish 2023 outcomes or direct causal attribution to the president.","CONEVAL reported that only 44.4% of indicators met 90-110% of target, the results matrix was considered not feasible, and some variables were not public or replicable."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cd5601d4566cbe20","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In a May 2023 PAN Senate communiqué, Senator Kenia López Rabadán alleged that AMLO minimized or covered up corruption involving contracts to his son's associates and other close relatives, and alleged nepotism, conflicts of interest, opacity, and unequal treatment of opposition and allies. She also alleged that the proposed electoral 'Plan B' concentrated power, bypassed parliamentary consultation requirements, and was accompanied by pressure on the Supreme Court.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","7B.2","7B.4","7B.5","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The allegations were made on 8 May 2023 and concern the administration's conduct during the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The claims are attributed to an opposition senator and concern alleged presidential conduct and administration practices.","limitations":["This is a partisan opposition statement, not an independent finding or adjudicated determination.","The document records allegations and criticism; it does not establish that the alleged corruption or unlawful pressure occurred."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b55f50402e2560c4","start_unit":6,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL reported that national labor poverty fell from 40.3% to 38.5% between the fourth quarters of 2021 and 2022, while real per-capita labor income rose 4.3% and employment increased by 1.7 million. Rural and urban labor poverty both declined, but the 2022 national rate remained above the pre-pandemic first-quarter 2020 level; women earned about 1.3 times less than men, and rural income was about half urban income.","question_ids":["5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence covers 2022 and was published in February 2023, providing the baseline entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The indicators describe national outcomes during AMLO's administration but do not by themselves establish presidential causation.","limitations":["The source reports aggregate labor outcomes and does not identify which policies caused them.","Persistent gender, rural-urban, and post-pandemic gaps qualify the favorable aggregate trend."]},{"source_id":"SRC-41df1275c66fe8c8","start_unit":1,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"INEGI reported preliminary real GDP growth of 3.3% nationally in 2023, with growth in 30 of 32 states; Quintana Roo, San Luis Potosí, and Oaxaca grew fastest, while Coahuila and Tamaulipas contracted. The release states that the estimates use the national accounts system, surveys, administrative records, and multiple federal and state data sources.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7","5B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly covers calendar year 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The figures describe economic performance during AMLO's final full year but do not establish that federal policy caused the state-level outcomes.","limitations":["The release is preliminary and subject to revision.","GDP growth alone does not establish distributional welfare, institutional quality, or presidential effectiveness."]},{"source_id":"SRC-03fd4f3bb212441b","start_unit":1,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"UN special procedures communicated allegations of repeated killings of civilians by military or National Guard personnel in Nuevo Laredo and alleged delayed, non-transparent, partial, or military-led investigations, scene manipulation, intimidation of victims' associates, and impunity. The communication notes that on 7 June 2023 AMLO stated an investigation had begun and that responsible personnel were about to be transferred to competent authorities; SEDENA later announced 16 military arrests and proceedings, but the communication found no evidence that competent civilian authorities participated in the investigation.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The communication was issued on 24 October 2023 and covers incidents from 2021-2023, including 2023 presidential and military responses.","ruler_attribution":"The president publicly stated that an investigation had begun; the alleged operational failures concern state security and investigative institutions.","limitations":["The UN communication expressly states that it does not prejudge the truth of the allegations.","It does not establish whether AMLO personally directed, knew of, or corrected the alleged abuses beyond the cited public statement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0fdf5cfbde266d7b","start_unit":2,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL reported that the 2023 federal budget contained 121 social programs and increased their nominal budget by 16.2% over 2022. The 15 continuing priority programs received a 28.1% nominal increase; 14 increased, while the National Reconstruction Program fell 36.22%. Programs linked to poverty reduction and social rights also received budget increases, and CONEVAL stated that evaluation evidence was relevant to budget allocation.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The analysis concerns the approved 2023 federal budget.","ruler_attribution":"The budget was submitted by the federal executive and approved by Congress during AMLO's administration.","limitations":["Budget allocations show planned resources, not completed implementation or outcomes.","The source does not establish whether evaluation evidence actually changed particular allocations or whether services improved."]},{"source_id":"SRC-263934a84cf853a8","start_unit":60,"end_unit":61,"fact_summary":"AP reported that Mexico ended 2022 with 7.82% annual inflation, including 14.14% food inflation. The central bank raised its policy rate to 10.5%, while the government temporarily removed import duties on some food categories; AP stated that it was unclear whether the measure was working.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","6B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence describes the macroeconomic shock entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The government measure is attributed to Mexico's administration; monetary-rate decisions are attributed to the central bank.","limitations":["The article does not evaluate the full fiscal, monetary, or distributional policy response.","The evidence is primarily about 2022 rather than outcomes during the whole 2023 period."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2f5bb8ae1f4f841e","start_unit":60,"end_unit":61,"fact_summary":"AP reported that Mexico's economy grew 3.6% in 2022 but slowed to 0.4% in the fourth quarter as high interest rates and inflation moderated consumption. Inflation stood at 7.82%, and analysts expected comparatively modest 2023 growth.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report establishes the macroeconomic conditions and expectations at the start of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The indicators describe Mexico during AMLO's administration but do not identify presidential causation.","limitations":["The article reports forecasts and aggregate outcomes rather than completed 2023 performance.","It does not evaluate the government's policy choices in detail."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4755738022be66db","start_unit":60,"end_unit":61,"fact_summary":"AP reported that remittances to Mexico rose 13.4% in 2022 to approximately $58.5 billion, a record amount, and exceeded nearly all other foreign-income sources. The article noted that the average transfer was $391, remittances had grown for 31 consecutive months, and slower global growth could reduce growth in 2023.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The evidence concerns 2022 remittances and the external economic conditions entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Remittances are primarily generated by migrants and external labor markets, not directly by presidential policy.","limitations":["The source does not show that the administration caused the increase or that remittances improved outcomes equally across households.","The article notes external dependence and possible slower growth."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0461ce165146c3b7","start_unit":30,"end_unit":34,"fact_summary":"UNAM's IISUE described a 2024 edited volume analyzing AMLO-era education policy, including reform, financing, management, the Nueva Escuela Mexicana, Universities for Wellbeing, scholarships, disability inclusion, teacher formation, curriculum, higher education, science, technology, and AI legislation. The catalog identifies the work as a multidisciplinary research-based assessment of advances, limitations, and unresolved challenges.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The source is a 2024 retrospective on 2018-2024 policies and therefore provides contextual evidence relevant to 2023, not a contemporaneous 2023 finding.","ruler_attribution":"The book explicitly analyzes policies implemented during AMLO's 2018-2024 administration.","limitations":["The supplied units provide the book description and contents, not the chapters' substantive findings.","No specific 2023 outcome or policy effect can be established from this catalog page alone."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4b42f64b3377abb8","start_unit":1,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"During a September 2023 visit invited by Mexico, the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention reported full access and cooperation, and acknowledged reforms including the accusatory criminal justice model, a National Registry of Detentions, restrictions on military jurisdiction, and some releases. It nevertheless found arbitrary detention widespread: mandatory pre-trial detention, militarized policing linked to violence and torture, unresolved complaints, excessive arrest violence, deficient records, pressure on judges, weak public defense, poor detention conditions, prolonged migrant and child detention, discrimination against indigenous people, and inadequate care for people with psychosocial disabilities.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","4B.7","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.8","6B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers the Working Group's September 2023 country visit and conditions observed or reported during that period.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern federal and state authorities under AMLO's administration; the invitation and official cooperation are specifically attributed to the government.","limitations":["The findings are preliminary and include information received from officials, civil society, and detainees.","They describe systemic conditions across multiple levels of government and do not assign personal responsibility to AMLO for each failure."]},{"source_id":"SRC-179202ba473bbcc6","start_unit":1,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The UN Working Group reported that Mexico invited its September 2023 visit, provided full and unimpeded access, and had adopted reforms including an accusatory justice model, detention registry, civilian jurisdiction for crimes against civilians, and some releases. The same preliminary findings stated that arbitrary detention remained widespread, with mandatory pre-trial detention, militarized policing associated with violence and torture, unresolved complaints, deficient arrest records, executive pressure on judges, weak legal assistance, abusive detention conditions, unlawful migrant and child detention, discrimination against indigenous people, and inadequate treatment for people with psychosocial disabilities.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","4B.7","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.8","6B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers the Working Group's September 2023 country visit and reported conditions during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern authorities operating under AMLO's administration; the invitation and cooperation are attributed to the Mexican government.","limitations":["This is a duplicate publication of the Working Group's preliminary findings and remains preliminary.","It does not establish personal presidential responsibility for every reported violation."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-263934a84cf853a8","SRC-2f5bb8ae1f4f841e","SRC-4755738022be66db"],"batch_limitations":["The three AP sources contain material facts in their article units, so they are included above; documents_with_no_material_fact is therefore empty."]}
